I've been farming this land since I was a girl, helping my mother and father. My husband goes to the city for work most of the year, so I manage the fields with help from my mother-in-law and sometimes neighbors during busy times. I don't read well, so I trust what the seed and fertilizer dealer in town tells me, and I watch what my neighbors do.

Here, everyone grows wheat then maize. That's what this land is good for. Wheat goes in the ground in October, you harvest in June, then you put maize in right away on the same field. Two crops off one piece of land — that's how we make it work. I have about 10 mu. I'll do wheat and maize on all of it, same as always.

For wheat, I'll use the improved seed variety the local store carries — everyone uses it, yields are decent. For maize I'll buy hybrid seed, that's what gives the best harvest. I don't save seed for maize anymore, haven't in years.

Fertilizer — I put down what the dealer says and what my neighbors use. More is safer in my mind. For irrigation, wheat needs water at winter, jointing, heading, and grain-fill — four times. Maize I'll irrigate if it doesn't rain enough in August, twice usually. We share the well with three other households.

I spray for weeds before the wheat tillers, then again for rust in spring. Maize I spray once for corn borer usually. I do rotary tillage before wheat planting. For maize I just direct seed into the wheat stubble — no-tillage saves time and my back.
